caveats:
The spatial accuracy and overall quality of this dataset depend on both the quality of the input data and the correctness of the edits made during processing. Temporal mismatches exist among the input datasets and reference sources, including satellite imagery, settlement polygons, and other health facility datasets used for comparison. In addition, spelling errors and naming inconsistencies may occur because place names can vary across data sources and local usage.

This dataset has not been fully validated by government officials or in-country stakeholders.

Benue, Cross River, Ebonyi, Plateau, and Taraba are included using their v1.0 boundaries and have not yet aligned with the updated boundaries of neighbouring states, the GRID3 NGA_Settlement Extent v4.1 data, or the current national boundary. Users may therefore find small gaps or slivers along the borders of these states and along the national boundary in these areas. These will be resolved in our next release. 

These data are part of ongoing work and should not be assumed to be fully accurate or complete. If users identify apparent errors or inconsistencies in the dataset, they should contact CIESIN at info@ciesin.columbia.edu.

The boundary edits included in this release are operational rather than authoritative. As ward boundary editing continues across Nigeria, corresponding changes to Local Government Area (LGA) and state boundaries may also be required to reflect the cumulative effects of these updates.

CIESIN, Columbia University, and its co-authors follow procedures designed to ensure that data disseminated by the project are of reasonable quality. If, despite these procedures, users encounter apparent errors or misstatements in the data, they should contact CIESIN, info@ciesin.columbia.edu.

CIESIN, Columbia University, its co-authors, and their sponsors do not guarantee the accuracy, reliability, or completeness of any data provided. We provide these data without warranty of any kind whatsoever, either expressed or implied, and shall not be liable for incidental, consequential, or special damages arising out of the use of any data provided.

Portions of this text were revised for clarity using a generative artificial intelligence tool. The final version was subsequently reviewed and approved by project staff.

name: grid3-nga-operational-wards-v4-0
notes:
The GRID3 NGA – Operational Wards v4.0 dataset provides operational ward boundary polygons for all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) of Nigeria.

This release updates the boundaries for 31 states and the FCT. Benue, Cross River, Ebonyi, Plateau and Taraba are included but have not been updated, and will be updated in the December release.  This version supersedes the previously published Version 3.0. The following changes were made:

- v4.0 includes major updates for Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Edo, Ekiti, Imo, Lagos, Ondo, and Rivers states (which had not been updated since v1.0) and supersedes v3.0 for the remaining 24 states, which have minor edits Ward boundaries were aligned to Small Settlement Areas (SSA) and Built-Up Areas (BUA) type settlement extents for all states and FCT
- State boundaries were aligned to SSA and BUA type settlement extents for all states and FCT, Abuja
- Ward boundaries were aligned to blocks for all states and FCT
- Ward boundaries modified based on PoI datasets (MLoS and health facility) and the boundaries aligned to major roads and water bodies (rivers and lakes for Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Edo, Ekiti, Imo, Lagos, Ondo, and Rivers)
- Kano Ward boundaries were modified based on National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) 2022 and 2025 version datasets
- The geometry for Ikuru ward in Andoni LGA, Rivers State, was removed in error and its name assigned to one part of Ataba 2 ward. Small gaps may also occur along the borders of Benue, Cross River, Ebonyi, Plateau and Taraba states, which still use v1.0 boundaries. Both issues will be corrected in our next release. 

GRID3 is continuously incorporating new input data into its products—this includes raw field data collected from health campaigns (often a few states at a time, at irregular intervals) and program data from GRID3 partners. When an update is made to one GRID3 product, GRID3 strives to include those updates in its other data products as quickly and efficiently as possible to ensure timely and seamless integration across all core spatial data. This v4.0 is the 3rd update to operational ward boundaries in 2026, covering a total of 31 states and FCT, and the next will constitute updates to operational ward boundaries for the entire country.

Each release uses the latest household registration, settlement, and health facility data, as well as aligns ward boundaries with other GRID3 core products, including settlement extents and blocks.

Dataset citation:

Center for Integrated Earth System Information (CIESIN), Columbia University 2026. GRID3 NGA - Operational Wards v4.0. New York: Columbia University. https://data.humdata.org/dataset/grid3-nga-operational-wards-v4-0. Accessed [DAY MONTH YEAR].

Contacts and data queries:

The authors of this dataset appreciate feedback regarding the data, including suggestions, discovery of errors, difficulties in using the data, and format preferences. For dataset-related questions, please send an email to: info@ciesin.columbia.edu

organization.description:
GRID3 works with countries in sub-Saharan Africa to generate, validate, and use core spatial datasets on population, settlements, subnational boundaries, and crucial infrastructure. We train and support stakeholders who use this information for analytics and decision-making, and work closely with local governments to improve national ownership and sustainability of the data.

We blend official data with data generated by novel approaches; our solutions draw on advanced data science and technology, participatory mapping, satellite imagery, and other innovations. GRID3 combines the expertise of leading technical partners to design pragmatic and responsive geospatial solutions that address the priority needs of each country.

Our work facilitates data-driven interventions that reach communities that need them the most. GRID3 solutions are valuable across multiple development sectors, from education to infrastructure. Our current focus is improving health interventions—particularly immunization coverage and malaria control—in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Nigeria.
